name: Stronghold Myre
description: Stronghold Myre is a temperate terrestrial world of ancient granite mountains, deep river valleys, and vast lowland bogs that stretch between weathered ranges. The mountains themselves are among the oldest geological formations cataloged in the sector, their rounded profiles and deep erosion patterns suggesting billions of years of slow, patient weathering. Dense rainforests cloak the valley slopes, their canopies so thick that the forest floor exists in permanent twilight.

Mist is the defining characteristic of Stronghold Myre's atmosphere -- it rises from the bogs at dawn, fills the valleys by midday, and clings to the mountain flanks until the weak evening sun burns it away. The air is perpetually damp, carrying the rich scent of peat and decomposing vegetation. Rainfall is frequent and gentle, sustaining the extraordinary density of plant life that covers every surface not submerged in bog water.

The flora of Stronghold Myre has evolved into a densely interconnected ecosystem where individual plants are difficult to distinguish from the collective. Root networks span kilometers, and chemical signaling between organisms suggests a level of coordinated response that borders on collective intelligence. Xenobotanists have documented instances of forest regions redirecting growth patterns in response to threats, effectively walling off damaged areas with accelerated woody growth.

As a colonization candidate, Stronghold Myre presents a paradox: it is habitable, resource-rich, and possessed of a mild climate, yet the density of its vegetation makes surface development extraordinarily labor-intensive. The bogs conceal treacherous depths, and the forest resists clearing with something that feels uncomfortably like intent. Those who have established research stations report a persistent sense of being watched -- not by fauna, but by the forest itself.
